v1_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-03), primarily because a billing-side defect — most plausibly a change to billing import validation rules — produces wrong bills even for the 59% of disputed accounts with accepted ACTUAL meter reads (E-04), while field route completion falling to 88% against a 95% target since August (E-01) adds a secondary stream of estimated-bill disputes. This is not a ticket-handling speed problem, since response times remain within SLA (E-02).
v2_problem: Monthly CRM dispute ticket volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03), substantially because billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3-based consumption history with no unit scaling; since v4.2 meter firmware (rollout 2026-06) reports register values in 0.1 m3 while legacy firmware reports in m3 (E-14), this mismatch causes valid AMI reads to be misclassified as high consumption and rejected (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution despite a valid read existing. This mechanism accounts for 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-12), coinciding with the August surge onset (E-13). The cause of the remaining dispute volume tied to ACTUAL-read bills (1785/3025, E-04) is not yet established and is not asserted here.
